answer:
Stage=result. Final natural-language hypothesis (3–6 sentences) below; per-domain summary table and primary answer included; artifacts under artifacts/. 

NOTE on plan-stage correction you should know: in my plan handoff I wrote "the 18 sign-flipping cases are all in Psychology." Re-running the audit on rr<0, the correct split is 15 in Psychology + 3 in Experimental Economics; by discipline this is 10 Social, 5 Cognitive, 3 Economics. The analysis, hypothesis, and headline.json now use the corrected split.

NATURAL-LANGUAGE HYPOTHESIS (for submission.answer):

Across all domains examined in this joined replication dataset (n=86 studies), original-study effect sizes tend to be larger than replication-study effect sizes on the Fisher-z scale. By replication project, both Psychology (n=68, mean Δ = fiso − fisr = +0.261, 95% percentile-bootstrap CI [0.193, 0.330], 85.3% of studies with fiso > fisr, paired Wilcoxon p < 0.0001) and Experimental Economics (n=18, mean Δ = +0.266, CI [0.116, 0.443], 83.3%, p = 0.0008) show positive shrinkage. The finer `discipline` axis splits Psychology into Cognitive (n=34, mean Δ = +0.289, median +0.249, 82.4%, p < 0.0001) and Social (n=34, mean Δ = +0.233, median +0.232, 88.2%, p < 0.0001), while Economics (n=18) is 1:1 with Experimental Economics in this dataset (mean Δ = +0.266, 83.3%, p = 0.0008). The conclusion is robust to whether the 18 sign-flipping replications (15 in Psychology, 3 in Experimental Economics; 10 Social, 5 Cognitive, 3 Economics) are included — every domain retains mean Δ > 0 and Wilcoxon p ≤ 0.01 when sign-flips are excluded. Headline, data-grounded: original effects exceed replication effects in every domain examined, with both replication projects and all three disciplines individually rejecting the null that fiso = fisr; Cognitive Psychology carries the largest absolute mean Fisher-z shrinkage (Δ = +0.289) and Social Psychology has the highest per-study rate of fiso > fisr (88.2%) because many of its replication Fisher-z values sit at or below zero.

PER-DOMAIN SUMMARY (Fisher-z paired comparison; incl. sign flips unless noted):

Primary axis — project.x (replication project):

|------------------------------|---|--------|-------------|----------|-------------|------------|
| Psychology                   | 68 |  0.261 | [0.193, 0.330] | 0.242 | 85.3% | <0.0001 |
|  ↳ Psychology, excl. flips   | 53 |  0.202 | [0.125, 0.278] | 0.207 | 81.1% | <0.0001 |
| Experimental Economics       | 18 |  0.266 | [0.116, 0.443] | 0.143 | 83.3% | 0.0008   |
|  ↳ Exp Econ, excl. flips     | 15 |  0.197 | [0.058, 0.370] | 0.106 | 80.0% | 0.0067   |

Secondary axis — discipline (with note Economics ⇔ Experimental Economics 1:1 in this dataset):
| scope                          | n | mean Δ | median Δ | % fiso>fisr | Wilcoxon p |
|--------------------------------|---|--------|----------|-------------|------------|
| Cognitive (Psychology)         | 34 |  0.289 | 0.249    | 82.4%       | <0.0001    |
|  ↳ Cognitive, excl. flips      | 29 |  0.224 | 0.230    | 79.3%       | 0.0001     |
| Social (Psychology)            | 34 |  0.233 | 0.232    | 88.2%       | <0.0001    |
|  ↳ Social, excl. flips         | 24 |  0.175 | 0.169    | 83.3%       | 0.0007     |
| Economics (≡ Experimental Economics) | 18 | 0.266 | 0.143 | 83.3% | 0.0008 |

Raw-correlation cross-check (ro − rr, signed; sanity row only):
| group                  | n | mean ro | mean rr | mean ro − rr |
|------------------------|---|---------|---------|--------------|
| Psychology             | 68 | 0.440 | 0.204 | 0.236 |
| Experimental Economics | 18 | 0.474 | 0.278 | 0.196 |
| Cognitive              | 34 | 0.533 | 0.285 | 0.249 |
| Social                 | 34 | 0.346 | 0.123 | 0.223 |
| Economics              | 18 | 0.474 | 0.278 | 0.196 |

payload.workflow: Loaded data/meta-regression_joined_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (86 rows × 60 columns, 0% missing on all core effect columns) and computed the per-study paired Fisher-z difference Δ = fiso − fisr. For each domain (project.x: Psychology/Experimental Economics; discipline: Cognitive/Social/Economics) I summarized Δ with n, mean, 95% percentile-bootstrap CI of the mean (10 000 resamples, α=0.05), median, the proportion of studies with fiso > fisr, and a paired two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test on Δ. I ran each domain twice — including the 18 sign-flips (replications whose fisr<0) and excluding them — to confirm the headline finding is not driven by sign-flips. Raw correlations (ro, rr) and Δ_r = ro − rr were computed as a sanity cross-check only. The supplied `relative_es` column was inspected (max|relative_es − rr/ro| = 0.944, 19 negative values) and excluded from the headline because it behaves like signed rr/ro rather than the magnitude-based ratio |rr|/|ro| described in the schema; this discrepancy is noted as a one-line caveat and does not affect the conclusion. The scatter of fiso vs fisr with the y = x reference and discipline-colored legend was rendered as a stdlib-SVG (artifacts/fiso_vs_fisr_scatter.svg) to satisfy the per-study visual requirement without external plotting libraries.
